title: Directed unweighted APSP below \(n^{5/2}\)
formal: Do there exist a constant \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) and a uniform bounded-error randomized word-RAM algorithm computing the full exact all-pairs distance matrix of every unweighted directed graph on \(n\) vertices in \(O(n^{5/2-\varepsilon})\) worst-case time?
definitions: The graph is given by its vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) arcs. It has no loops and at most one arc per ordered pair; opposite arcs are allowed. Every arc has length one. For each ordered pair \((u,v)\in V\times V\), output the minimum number of arcs on a directed path from \(u\) to \(v\), or infinity if no path exists; diagonal entries are zero. The output is an explicit \(n\times n\) array. Use a uniform word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_{2}(n+2)\rceil\), for a fixed positive integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm and large enough for its addresses and input values. Unit-cost instructions are word reads/writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Multiword computation is charged by its component instructions. The fixed finite program receives no advice or precomputed tables; all initialization, preprocessing and output writes count. Randomness consists of independent uniform random words, each generated at unit cost. On every input, the whole output must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). The time bound holds for every random execution, including unsuccessful ones. The constant \(\varepsilon\) and all other constants are independent of the graph. No assumption about the matrix multiplication exponent \(\omega\), or about additive combinatorics, is included in the claim.

context_blocks.text: Even without numerical weights, directed all-pairs distances have resisted the exponent improvements available for undirected graphs. Direction alone preserves a substantial fine-grained bottleneck.

Chan, Vassilevska Williams and Xu explain why the established directed bounds still encounter \(n^{5/2}\) when \(\omega=2\), and develop reductions relating this problem to small-integer min-plus products.
Fischer gives conditional equivalences among APSP hypotheses in 2026, assuming \(\omega=2\) and an additive-combinatorics assumption. Those equivalences do not supply the algorithm requested here.

why: This is a central fine-grained benchmark for whether directed distance computation has an exponent barrier even when every edge has unit length.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

sentences: Directed unweighted all-pairs shortest paths asks for every ordered-pair distance when each arc has length one.
The full distance matrix must be output explicitly.
The question asks for a fixed exponent improvement below \(n^{5/2}\) with bounded-error randomization.
The target makes no assumption about matrix multiplication or additive combinatorics.
Recent conditional equivalences connect this barrier to other APSP hypotheses without resolving it.
